Preset.balanced.Tagline: Recommended default · same result and speed as the old Kraken 7
Preset.balanced.Detail: Kraken level 4 (Normal) — the very encoder the 2.0.0 engine used for its Sony-standard "Kraken 7": identical package size, same speed, plus the new engine's dedup/layout gains. The default.

Help.Extract.Title: Extract mode
Help.Extract.1: • Switch to Extract PKG in the header, then pick or drop a .pkg: the app reads the FIH/CNT headers, every param.json field, the icon and lists all files inside the PPR-PFS image.
Help.Extract.2: • Filter, tick files/folders and extract the selection or the whole package. PLAINTEXT_NOAUTH packages are read straight from the .pkg in 4 MiB chunks (no image rebuild); Native packages are first decrypted to the temp folder.
Help.Extract.3: • Signed retail packages are information-only. The extracted app tree is in Sony layout (sce_sys/param.json, icon0.png, playgo… merged from the CNT) and can be rebuilt directly; the raw CNT / SI exports are optional. CLI: fpkg-cli pkg-info / pkg-list / pkg-extract.

Help.Title: User guide
Help.Subtitle: Build debug FPKG packages for PS5 from an app folder — on macOS, Windows and Linux
Help.Quick.Title: Quick start
Help.Quick.1: Prepare the extracted PS5 app folder: it must contain a sce_sys folder (param.json, icon0.png…) and eboot.bin. You can also pick a GP5 project (.gp5) from Publishing Tools / fpkg-gui — the package then contains exactly the files the project lists.
Help.Quick.2: In step 1 click Browse… or drop the folder onto the window. Content ID, title, version, size and junk files are detected automatically.
Help.Quick.3: Choose the output folder for the .pkg. The temp folder is suggested on the same volume to avoid cross-volume copies, and free space is checked for you.
Help.Quick.4: Pick a speed preset in step 3 (Fast · Standard · Smallest · Maximum). Standard (level 4) is the default: it is the same encoder the 2.0.0 engine used for its Kraken 7, so you get the old size at the old speed. Smallest (level 7, Optimal) is about 3 % smaller but 5–6× slower. Or open the advanced options.
Help.Quick.5: Click Build PKG (Ctrl/⌘+B or F5). Watch the progress, remaining time and log; when finished the package structure is verified and the result is shown.
Help.Speed.Title: Speed & optimisation
Help.Speed.1: • The built-in Kraken encoder uses every CPU core; threads = 0 means automatic. On Windows, native Oodle is preferred when libScePubTools.dll is present.
Help.Speed.2: • The default preset is Standard (Kraken level 4) — in the 2.0.0 engine levels 4–7 all used this Normal encoder, so it reproduces the old "Kraken 7" result at the old speed. Smallest (level 7, Optimal3) shrinks the package by roughly 3 % more but takes 5–6× longer on real game data; Fast (level 2) is for quick tests. Already-compressed files (video, audio, textures) are stored raw automatically.
Help.Speed.3: • Uncompressed mode builds about twice as fast but produces a noticeably larger package — handy for quick tests.
Help.Speed.4: • Put the temp folder on an SSD, on the same volume as the output. You need roughly 1.1× the source size free for the temp image and 1.1× for the .pkg.
Help.Speed.5: • The app keeps the computer awake while building (caffeinate on macOS, SetThreadExecutionState on Windows, systemd-inhibit on Linux) — disable it in the advanced options if you prefer.
Help.Speed.6: • Post-build SHA-256 re-reads the entire .pkg; for packages of tens of GB enable it only when needed.
Help.Notes.Title: Important notes
Help.Notes.1: • The output and temp folders must not be inside the source folder.
Help.Notes.2: • The result is a debug FPKG (FIH, signed byte 0x00) — it only installs on a PS5 with debug mode enabled.
Help.Notes.3: • On macOS, Finder creates .DS_Store files; the app detects them and offers to remove them so they do not end up in the package.
Help.Notes.4: • The passcode defaults to 32 zeros — only change it when you really need to.
Help.Notes.5: • Enable deterministic builds to reproduce an identical package from the same source.
Help.Notes.6: • Use the fpkg-cli command-line tool for batch or automated builds (see README).

Help.About.Body: PSVIETHOA FPKG Builder is a cross-platform (macOS & Windows) application written in C# / .NET with Avalonia UI, developed by PSVIETHOA (Nguyễn Thanh Sơn & Ngô Phi Phương) on top of Drakmor's LibProsperoPkg 1.2.0 library: debug FPKG creation, PlayGo, Kraken/Oodle compression, SDK override and result verification.

Cli.Help:
PSVIETHOA FPKG Builder CLI — build PS5 FPKG (FIH debug) packages from an app folder.

USAGE
  fpkg-cli build --source <dir> --output <dir> [options]
  fpkg-cli inspect <source dir|.exfat|.ffpfsc|.ffpkg|.gp5> [--output <dir>]
  fpkg-cli verify <file.pkg> [--sha256] [--full] [--passcode X]
  fpkg-cli clean-junk <dir> [--dry-run]
  fpkg-cli info
  fpkg-cli check-update
  fpkg-cli install-dokan                (Windows) install the bundled Dokan driver for copy-free mounting
  fpkg-cli dlc-from-ini <folder|image|dlc_emu.ini> --output <dir>      build one DLC package per entry of dlc_emu.ini
  fpkg-cli pkg-info <file.pkg> [--passcode X] [--sha256]
  fpkg-cli pkg-list <file.pkg> [--include <glob>]...
  fpkg-cli pkg-extract <file.pkg> --output <dir> [--include <glob>]... [--cnt] [--no-sce-sys] [--passcode X] [--threads N] [--temp <dir>]
  fpkg-cli pkg-dlc-template <file.pkg> [--output <dir>] [--passcode X]

OPTIONS for build
  -s, --source <dir|.exfat|.ffpkg|.gp5> App folder (contains sce_sys/), an exFAT/.ffpfsc/.ffpkg image, or a GP5 project.
  -o, --output <dir>       Output folder for the .pkg.
      --temp <dir>         Temporary folder (default: same volume as the output).
  -c, --content-id <id>    36-character Content ID (default: read from sce_sys/param.json).
  -t, --title <name>       App title (when param.json has none).
  -v, --version <NN.NNN.NNN>
      --kind app|homebrew|dlc          Package type (default app).
      --image plaintext|native        Outer image mode (default plaintext).
      --preset fast|balanced|smallest|maximum  Speed/compression preset (default balanced = Standard: level 4, the old engine's "Kraken 7"; aliases sony|standard; smallest = level 7 Optimal, slow).
      --backend auto|builtin|pubtools|none
      --level <-4..9>      Kraken level (default 4).
      --threads <n>        Compression threads (0 = automatic).
      --playgo <1..255>    Fallback PlayGo chunks (default 100; a source playgo-chunk.dat supplies the count).
      --sdk <1..11>        Override the SDK major version.
      --passcode <32 chars>
      --dll <path>         libScePubTools.dll (Windows only).
      --sha256             Compute SHA-256 after building.
      --full-verify        Decrypt and test-decompress every file after building (the quick content check always runs).
      --no-deterministic   Disable deterministic builds.
      --clean-junk         Delete .DS_Store/Thumbs.db… from the source first.
      --no-sleep-guard     Do not keep the computer awake.
      --quiet              Print only progress and the result.
      --exfat auto|mount|extract   .exfat/.ffpfsc images: copy-free mount (hdiutil on macOS, Dokan on Windows) or extract to the temp folder (default auto).
      --pfs v2|v3          PFS compression format (default v2; v3 unlocks shuffles/region hints).
      --block-size <KiB>   Kraken block size 128..256 (default 256).
      --shuffle <pattern>  PFS v3 shuffle: none, PredictForStructs, PredictForBc1..5, Shuffle116, …
      --shuffle-analysis   Automatic shuffle analysis (PFS v3).
      --shuffle-prediction-level <-4..9|auto>
      --skip-pfs-input-check   Skip the PFS v3 input compatibility check (expert).
      --keep-drm           Keep applicationDrmType as in the source (default: forced to "standard").
      --keep-ampr          Keep the AMPR emu leftovers (ampr_emu.index) in the package.
      --keep-playgo        Keep the source's sce_sys/playgo* files in the package (default: dropped and regenerated).
      --keep-version-uri   Keep versionFileUri in param.json (default: cleared to "").
      --keep-attribute3    Keep attribute3 in param.json (default: set to 0).
      --keep-required-fw   Keep requiredSystemSoftwareVersion (default: lowered to the game's SDK when higher).
      --strip-dlc-emu      Remove the DLC emulator (dlc_emu.ini + fakelib modules) from the package (default: kept).
      --overwrite / --keep-existing   Same-named package in the output folder: replace it, or keep (rename) the old one.
      --no-layout-optimization Disable block coalescing / alignment adjustment.
      --source-mode auto|folder|gp5   Source reading mode (default auto: GP5 when present).
      --project <file.gp5> GP5 project for --source-mode gp5.
      --lang vi|en         Message language (or the FPKG_LANG environment variable).

Help.Notes.7: • A source can be an exFAT disk image (.exfat) or a .ffpfsc container (the PFSC-compressed exFAT image some dump tools produce). On macOS the app mounts .exfat images with hdiutil and builds directly (no copy); on Windows click "Enable direct mounting" in the advanced options (the Dokan driver is bundled, one administrator prompt) to mount the same way — a read-only virtual drive served by the app that also handles .ffpfsc, hides junk files and applies the DRM fix on the drive. When mounting is impossible (no Dokan, .ffpfsc on macOS, junk files on macOS) the app extracts the image to the temp folder and cleans up afterwards. A GP5 project (.gp5) is read exactly as written — Normal layout (rootdir + exclude masks) or Flat layout (explicit file list); relative paths resolve from the folder containing the .gp5, and the output / temp folders must be outside both the project root and the folder holding the .gp5 (the output folder is suggested right next to it).
Help.Notes.8: • PFS v3 + automatic shuffle analysis optimises texture compression through a permutation-selection pass: it is very time-consuming and only fully effective at Kraken level 9 (the Maximum preset). PFS v3 packages need PS5 firmware 7.00 or newer — on older firmware the game may not launch, so keep PFS v2 unless you need the extra savings.
Help.Notes.9: • Every time it starts, the app checks GitHub Releases (can be turned off in the advanced options). When a newer version exists the header shows a green badge, the ↻ button gets a dot and a dialog asks whether to download it; the ↻ button checks manually at any time. Nothing is ever downloaded automatically.

Help.Credits.Thanks: Thanks to the PS5 homebrew community and everyone who contributed to LibProsperoPkg.

Advanced.PfsHint: PFS v3 unlocks pre-compression shuffles and automatic shuffle analysis (texture optimisation) for smaller packages; v2 ignores those options. Both are independent of the SDK version, but PFS v3 needs PS5 firmware 7.00 or newer.
Advanced.PfsV3Firmware: PFS v3 packages require PS5 firmware 7.00 or newer — games may fail to launch on older firmware. Keep PFS v2 for maximum compatibility.
Advanced.BlockSizeHint: 128–256 KiB; 256 KiB is the SDK-compatible default. Smaller blocks use less RAM but compress slightly worse.
Advanced.ShuffleHint: De-interleaves bytes by structure before compression so similar bytes sit together. The "predict" patterns choose between identity and the matching shuffle automatically.
Advanced.ShuffleAnalysisHint: Texture compression optimisation: tries every byte-permutation (shuffle) pattern per block during the compression pass and keeps the smallest result. Very time-consuming, and only fully effective at Kraken level 9.
Advanced.ShuffleLevelWarning: Shuffle analysis only takes full effect at Kraken level 9 — set level 9 (or pick the Maximum preset) to get the texture optimisation.
Advanced.SkipPfsCheck: Skip the PFS input compatibility check (expert)
Advanced.SkipPfsCheckHint: Only if you know what you are doing (PFS v3). ELF/SELF/PRX/SPRX files stay raw regardless.
Advanced.LayoutHint: Coalesces movable blocks and adjusts alignment like Publishing Tools to shrink the image (recommended).
Advanced.ForceDrmHint: applicationDrmType in the package is set to "standard" — packages built with "free" DRM show a lock on the PS5 and refuse to start. Engine 0.6.8 does this in memory; the source param.json is never touched.
Preset.maximum.Name: Maximum
Preset.maximum.Detail: Kraken level 9 + PFS v3 + automatic shuffle analysis (byte-permutation texture optimisation) — the smallest package the engine can make, by far the slowest; needs PS5 firmware 7.00 or newer.
Plan.Pfs: PFS {0} · Kraken block {1} KiB · shuffle: {2} · layout optimisation: {3}
Plan.DiskFullCancel: Build cancelled because the disk is full.
Plan.DrmPolicyOff: DRM: applicationDrmType is kept as in the source.
Plan.DrmPolicyOn: DRM: applicationDrmType is forced to "standard" (done by the engine in memory, the source is unchanged).
Plan.ShuffleLevel: Shuffle analysis is enabled at Kraken level {0}: the texture optimisation only takes full effect at level 9.
Plan.PfsV3Firmware: PFS v3 package: requires PS5 firmware 7.00 or newer; older firmware may refuse to launch the game.
Val.KrakenBlock: The Kraken block size must be between 128 and 256 KiB.
Val.ShufflePrediction: The shuffle prediction level must be between -4 and 9 (or automatic).
Val.ProjectMissing: GP5 mode needs an existing .gp5 project file.
Advanced.ExFatHint.Hdiutil: Mounting with hdiutil is fastest: no copy, no extra disk space. Extracting needs extra free space equal to the data in the image but skips junk files automatically.
Advanced.ExFatHint.Dokan: Dokan {0} is ready: .exfat / .ffpfsc images are mounted as a read-only virtual drive and the library reads straight from the image — no copy, no extra space; junk files are hidden and the DRM fix is applied on the virtual drive.
Advanced.ExFatHint.NoMount: This system cannot mount images, so the app extracts them to the temp folder (needs extra free space equal to the data in the image; junk files are skipped).
Advanced.DokanCallout: Install Dokan (free, open source) so Windows can mount .exfat / .ffpfsc images directly like macOS: no extracting hundreds of GB to the temp folder, no extra disk space. Click "Check again" after installing.
Plan.MountedVia: Mounted the image at {0} via {1} — reading straight from the image, no copy.
Plan.MountJunkHidden: OS junk files (.DS_Store, ._*, Thumbs.db…) are hidden from the virtual drive.
Plan.MountNeedsDokan: Dokan is not installed on this Windows system, so the image cannot be mounted — extracting to the temp folder (install Dokan to skip this step).
Advanced.DokanCalloutBundled: Mounting images directly like on macOS needs the Dokan driver (open source, bundled with this package — version {0}). Click "Enable direct mounting": Windows asks for administrator rights once, nothing to download or install by hand. Without it, images are still extracted to the temp folder as before.
Dokan.ConfirmBody:
The app will install the bundled Dokan driver {0} (open source, LGPL) silently through the Windows installer. Windows will ask for administrator rights once.

Afterwards .exfat / .ffpfsc images are mounted as a read-only virtual drive and packages are built straight from the image — no extraction, no extra disk space.
Dokan.OfferTitle: Build straight from the image, without extracting?
Dokan.OfferBody:
This PC has no Dokan driver, so the image will be extracted to the temp folder (extra free space equal to the data in the image).

The Dokan {0} installer is bundled — install it now (one administrator prompt) to mount images directly like on macOS? You can also enable it later in the advanced options.
Dokan.Installing: Installing the Dokan driver… please confirm the Windows administrator prompt.
Dokan.Installed: Dokan driver {0} is ready. From now on .exfat / .ffpfsc images are mounted as a virtual drive and built straight from the image.
Dokan.RebootRequired: The Dokan driver is installed but Windows needs a restart before it can be used. After restarting, the app mounts images automatically.
Dokan.Failed:
The installer returned code {0}. {1}

You can install it manually from the Dokan page and click "Check again". Without Dokan the app still builds packages by extracting the image.
Dokan.NotBundled: This package does not include the Dokan installer. Download it from the Dokan page and click "Check again".
Cli.DokanWindowsOnly: install-dokan is only available on Windows.
Cli.DokanInstalled: Dokan {0} installed — copy-free mounting is ready.
Cli.DokanReboot: Dokan installed — restart Windows before using it.
Cli.DokanNotBundled: redist/Dokan_x64.msi was not found next to the application.

Dokan.AutoInstallLog: Enabling direct mounting: installing the bundled Dokan driver {0} (Windows asks for administrator rights once)…
Dokan.CancelledLog: Dokan driver not installed (administrator rights not granted) — images will be extracted; enable it later in the advanced options.
Plan.AmprRemoved: AMPR emu: removed {0} from the package (the engine always drops fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx, so the index file is useless). Nothing in the source folder is touched.
Advanced.RemoveAmprHint: Drops ampr_emu.index (and fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx) from the package. Engine 0.6.8 drops both by itself as well; the tool drops them once more to be safe. Nothing in your source folder is deleted or edited; the files are only left out of the package.
Conflict.Title: The output folder already has a package with this name
Cli.ConflictNeedChoice: Use --overwrite to replace it or --keep-existing to rename the old one.
Advanced.RemovePlayGoHint: Every file in sce_sys whose name starts with "playgo" (playgo-chunk.dat, playgo-hash-table.dat, playgo-ficm.dat, playgo-scenario.json, playgo-manifest.xml…) is left out of the package. Engine 0.6.8 regenerates every PlayGo table anyway; when these files are kept it only reads the chunk and scenario counts from playgo-chunk.dat. On (default) uses the fallback chunk count. Off keeps the original counts, and broken files are still dropped so the build does not stop. Only sce_sys is affected, and nothing in your source folder is deleted or edited.
Plan.PlayGoRemoved: PlayGo: left the dump's {0} out of the package; the engine generates a fresh PlayGo set matching the image (Drakmor: stale playgo* files make games throw an error on launch).
PlayGo.Regenerate: PlayGo: the source's {0} playgo* files are dropped; the engine generates 1 scenario / {1} chunks.
Build.ResetDefaultsTip: Put every packaging option (preset, compression, PFS, block size, DRM, playgo, AMPR, PlayGo, SDK…) back to its default. Paths, package info, language, theme and history are kept.
Reset.Title: Restore default options?
Reset.Body:
Every packaging option goes back to its default: Standard preset (Kraken 4), PFS v2, 256 KiB blocks, no shuffle, DRM "standard" on, drop old playgo* on, clear versionFileUri on, clear attribute3 on, keep DLC emulator on, AMPR cleanup on, 100 PlayGo chunks, lower requiredSystemSoftwareVersion to the SDK on, a passcode of 32 zeros, deterministic build on, SHA-256 off, full verification off, sleep guard on, update check on.

Kept: source / output / temp paths, the package info and SDK version read from the source, language, theme, history and window size.
Dlc.SkippedWithData: Skipped {0}: this DLC ships its own data ({1}), so it must be packaged from the real data, not as an empty package.
Dlc.Title: DLC found — build separate DLC packages?
Plan.DlcEmuKept: DLC emu: dlc_emu.ini and the fakelib modules stay inside the package (default).
Plan.DlcEmuRemoved: DLC emu: removed {0} from the package as you chose — the DLC unlocks through the separate DLC packages (button on the source card).
Plan.EmptyFolderDropped: Folder {0} has no files left after the cleanup — left out of the package (recreated in the source after the build).
Cli.DlcNeedIni: No dlc_emu.ini found in the given source.
Advanced.KeepDlcEmu: Keep the DLC emulator in the package
Plan.PatchDrm: param.json: applicationDrmType "{0}" → "{1}" (avoids the lock icon on the PS5).
Plan.PatchVersionUri: param.json: versionFileUri "{0}" → "" (drops the original package's version-check URL).
Plan.PatchAttribute3: param.json: attribute3 {0} → 0 (clears the original package's attribute flags, per the PlayGo fix guide).
Plan.ParamPatchFailed: Could not patch param.json ({0}) — building with the source's own values.
Plan.MountParamOverlay: param.json patched on the virtual drive, the image itself untouched: {0}
Plan.VersionUriPolicy: param.json: versionFileUri will be cleared (a self-built package does not update through the original URL).
Plan.Attribute3Policy: param.json: attribute3 will be set to 0 — the documented flags (video-out, 120 Hz / HFR, VRR or Auto Scaling, PS5 Pro) are switched off in the package too. Turn this option off if your game runs fine without it.
Plan.Gp5CleanupFailed: Could not patch the GP5 project to drop those files ({0}) — building with every file in the project.
Advanced.PlayGoFixTitle: PlayGo & param.json fix ("application error" when the game starts)
Advanced.PlayGoFixHint: An FPKG is one single unified image while PlayGo is built around chunk-based installs, so the dump's PlayGo data makes the PS5 look for chunks that do not exist and throw an application error the moment you press play. Per Drakmor, dropping the playgo* files clears that error. Note: a game that hangs on the splash screen WITHOUT an error (Stellar Blade, Ghost of Yōtei) has a different, kernel-side problem that none of these options can fix.
Advanced.ClearVersionUriHint: Sets versionFileUri to an empty string in the package: a self-built package does not update through the original package's version-check URL. On by default. The param.json in your source folder is not edited.
Advanced.ClearAttribute3: Clear the attribute3 flags in param.json
Advanced.ClearAttribute3Hint: Sets attribute3 to 0 while building — the guide's "uncheck the PlayGo flags" step. No public documentation maps a PlayGo bit in attribute3, so the whole field is set to 0: the documented flags (video-out info, 120 Hz / HFR, VRR or Auto Scaling, PS5 Pro support) are switched off in the package too. If the dump has no playgo* files at all this step fixes nothing — switch it off to keep those flags.
Advanced.RemovePlayGo: Drop every sce_sys/playgo* file of the dump
Plan.Mirror: The source folder is READ-ONLY: every change (dropped files, patched param.json) happens in the temporary mirror {0}, removed when the build finishes.
Plan.MirrorFailed: Could not build the mirror folder here ({0}).
Plan.Gp5Redirect: GP5 project: building from the temporary copy {0}; your own .gp5 file is only read.
Val.MirrorRequired: The mirror folder could not be built (neither in the temporary folder nor in the system temporary folder), so files cannot be dropped and param.json cannot be patched while leaving your source folder untouched. The build was stopped rather than produce a wrong package. The log names the file and the error. This usually happens when the source sits on a network drive; copy the source to a local drive, or switch the PlayGo fix options off and try again.
Plan.MirrorForWrites: The library writes into the folder it reads (generating a missing param.json, or saving compression region hints), so a mirror is built anyway to keep your source folder read-only.
Reset.DoneSdk: All packaging options were restored to their defaults; the SDK stays with the source: SDK {0}.
Plan.JunkSkipped: OS junk: {0} file(s) left out of the package (.DS_Store, ._*, Thumbs.db…). Your source folder is untouched.
Step1.PickFfpkgTip: A UFS2 image (FreeBSD filesystem) holding the game's app folder. Neither macOS nor Windows can mount UFS, so the tool reads it itself and extracts to the temporary folder.
PlayGo.Import: PlayGo: chunk count taken from the source's playgo-chunk.dat ({0} chunks / {1} scenarios); the engine regenerates every table to match the new image.
PlayGo.ImportScenarios: PlayGo: {0} fallback chunks, {1} scenarios from playgo-scenario.json; the engine regenerates every table.
PlayGo.Invalid: PlayGo: {0} is invalid and will be left out (the engine stops on a broken file) — using {1} chunks.
Plan.PlayGoInvalid: PlayGo: {0} is invalid for the engine and is left out of the package (keeping it would stop the build). The source file is not touched.
Plan.PatchRequiredFw: param.json: requiredSystemSoftwareVersion {0} → {1} (lowered to the game's SDK, per fpkg-gui 0.6.8).
Plan.RequiredFwSdk: requiredSystemSoftwareVersion: set by the engine to the selected SDK {0}.
Plan.RequiredFwLower: requiredSystemSoftwareVersion: lowered to the game's SDK when it is higher.
Plan.RequiredFwKeep: requiredSystemSoftwareVersion: kept as in the source.
Plan.VerifyPolicyQuick: Post-build check: structure + quick contents (CNT signature, PlayGo layout, NAPS, inodes).
Plan.VerifyPolicyFull: Post-build check: full — decrypts and test-decompresses every file in memory.
Plan.VerifyingFull: Running the full package check (test-decompressing every file in memory)…
Plan.VerifiedQuick: Quick content check passed all {0} checks ({1}).
Plan.VerifiedFull: Full content check passed all {0} checks ({1}).
Verify.ContentFailed: The built package failed the content check: {0}
Advanced.LowerRequiredFw: Lower requiredSystemSoftwareVersion to the game's SDK
Advanced.LowerRequiredFwHint: Per fpkg-gui 0.6.8: the minimum system version in the package is lowered to the SDK the game was built with when it is higher, so the package installs on lower firmware. Applies only while keeping the game's SDK; picking an SDK makes the engine use that SDK instead.
Advanced.FullVerifyHint: Decrypts and test-decompresses every file in memory and checks every block against its hash table — takes about as long as reading the whole package. The quick check (CNT signature, PlayGo layout, NAPS, inodes) always runs.
Extract.VerifyQuickTip: Reads the package metadata: segment ranges, CNT signature, the complete PlayGo layout, outer PFS superblock, NAPS, inner PFS inodes and the SI directory. Takes seconds and writes nothing to disk.
Extract.VerifyFullTip: The quick check plus decrypting every outer PFS block, matching it against imagedigs.dat and test-decompressing every file in memory. Takes about as long as reading the whole package and writes nothing to disk.
Extract.VerifyFailed: The package FAILED the check — {0} problem(s):
Plan.MirrorFallback: The temporary folder {0} cannot hold links (usually an exFAT/FAT32 or network drive) — building the (tiny) mirror folder in {1} instead; the build's temporary data still goes to the temporary folder you chose.
Plan.AppliedInPlace: Dropped/patched files directly in the extracted copy in the temporary folder ({0}); the original source is not touched.
Plan.SplitDrives: Temporary and output folders are on different drives: temporary {0}, output {1}.
Plan.FatVolume: {0} is on a FAT/FAT32 drive: it cannot hold files of 4 GB or more, so the temporary image or the .pkg of a large game will fail. Use an NTFS, exFAT or APFS drive.
Disk.Fat: Warning: {0} is a FAT/FAT32 drive and cannot hold files of 4 GB or more.
Plan.AppleDoubleRemoved: Removed {0} AppleDouble "._*" files that macOS creates on exFAT/FAT drives ({1}) so they do not end up in the package.
DlcTemplate.NotEmpty: The folder {0} is not empty — a DLC template needs an empty folder.
DlcTemplate.NotDlc: A template can only be exported from a DLC package with data (additional content with data).
DlcTemplate.Tip: Exports the sce_sys files needed to rebuild this DLC package (param.json, license, icon…) and a <Content ID>.gp5 project (DLC type, Content ID, passcode, entitlement key, the original PlayGo layout) to a "<package>-dlc-template" folder next to the .pkg. The payload is not copied. Put the DLC data in that folder, then pick the .gp5 as the source to build the package again.
